thread:
maria: FYI the sample app on Next.js Edge errors with \"require() of ES Module\" when importing our SDK. Happens during Vercel Edge deploy.

sam: Ugh, seen that. Usually package.json conditional exports are confusing for edge/workers. Edge needs the ESM path, but bundlers sometimes pick the CJS one. :thinking_face:

lee: Can you paste the error stack? quick guess: bundler resolving 'main' -> cjs. Next edge runtime expects native ESM.

maria: Error: TypeError: require is not defined (stack points to node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/cjs/index.js). Build shows webpack/rollup resolving to main.

anya: We should publish with explicit exports that include a worker/default fallback. Example I used elsewhere: 

```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
      "worker": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  },
  "main": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

sam: That helps but note: some bundlers ignore the non-standard \"worker\" condition. For maximum compatibility do: 
- exports with \"import\" and \"require\"
- top-level \"module\" and \"main\" for older tools
- ensure package.json has a top-level \"types\" pointing to d.ts

lee: Also consider shipping an explicit \"exports\" subpath for edge-friendly entry, e.g. \"\"./edge\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\"\". Then sample apps can `import {Client} from '@redwood/inference/edge'` to be explicit.

maria: Good call. That would avoid relying on bundler heuristics.

anya: Typings: TypeScript sometimes picks up types from CJS build if d.ts locations mismatch. Keep a single d.ts output in dist/index.d.ts and point top-level \"types\" to it. If consumers use path imports, publish matching `dist/edge/index.d.ts` for the subpath.

sam: Another gotcha: auth & retry behavior differs between Node and Edge. Our Node SDK uses node-fetch + AbortController semantics; Edge uses native fetch. Retries that inspect `err.code` break on Edge since fetch throws TypeError for network errors. We need an isomorphic retry wrapper.

lee: Proposal: implement a tiny adapter layer: 

```js
// runtime-adapter.js (internal)
export function isEdge() { return typeof process === 'undefined' || !!globalThis?.WebSocket; }
export const fetchImpl = isEdge() ? globalThis.fetch : nodeFetch;
```

Then retry logic should base on response status and safe network-check helpers rather than Node-only properties.

maria: For sample apps we should update quickstart to import the edge entry explicitly and mention the adapter. Right now our Next.js example just uses `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` which pulls CJS in some setups.

anya: Short-term fix for onboarding: add a line in README and the Next.js sample: `import { Client } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` and update the example package.json for Next Edge.

sam: Long-term: our publish pipeline should produce: 
- dist/esm (for browsers/edge)
- dist/cjs (for node require)
- dist/edge (optional but mirrors esm)
- export map with subpaths and conditions
- types at dist/index.d.ts + subpath .d.ts files

maria: Is there any risk of breakage for existing users if we add an \"edge\" subpath?

lee: Minimal. It’s additive. Breaking changes come from removing main/module or moving files. We should keep main/module and maintain semver.

deploy-bot: deploy-preview created for fix/edge-publish-playbook #142 (staging). :rocket:

anya: Also add a test in our SDK CI that installs the package from the built tarball into a tiny Next.js app using Edge runtime and runs a smoke import test. Catches regressions early.

sam: Agreed. I'll open a PR with package.json export map + README edits and add the CI smoke test.

maria: Thanks — that should unblock onboarding and reduce support tickets. :thumbsup:

lee: If anyone wants to pair on the PR ping me. I can help with the publish workflow changes.

maria: pinging @sam @lee to review the sample app PR once it's up.

anya: One more thing — update changelog to document the new edge entrypoint so customers using custom bundlers know about the path.

sam: Will do.
